title: Bonus Episode: Driverless Cars and Body-less Therapy with Arnon Rolnick, PhD

sentences.en: Hey, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: It's Caitlin Luna, host of Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我是《心理学谈话》的主持人凯特琳·卢娜。

sentences.en: This episode was recorded during
sentences.zh: 本期节目是在

sentences.en: APA's Technology, Mind, and Society conference held in October 2019 in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 2019年10月于华盛顿特区举行的美国心理学会（APA）“技术、思维与社会”会议期间录制的。

sentences.en: I was away on maternity leave during that time, so my colleague Kim Mills was a guest hoSt.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在休产假，所以由我的同事金·米尔斯担任客座主持。

sentences.en: We hope you like this episode.
sentences.zh: 希望大家喜欢这一期节目。

sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a biweekly podcast from the American Psychological
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是一档由美国心理学会制作的双周播客，

sentences.en: Association that explores the connections between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Kim Mills, and I'm coming to you from APA's annual Technology, Mind, and Society
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯，现在正在华盛顿特区参加美国心理学会举办的年度“技术、思维与社会”

sentences.en: conference in Washington, D.C., a cross-disciplinary meeting to discuss psychology's role in developing
sentences.zh: 会议。这是一场跨学科会议，旨在探讨心理学在开发

sentences.en: and advancing everything from virtual reality to artificial intelligence to the Internet of Things.
sentences.zh: 和推进从虚拟现实、人工智能到物联网等各个领域中的作用。

sentences.en: Have you ever wondered why drivers don't get car sick?
sentences.zh: 你有没有想过为什么开车的人不会晕车？

sentences.en: And if you've ever been seasick, are you curious to know what causes it and what, if anything, can be done to stave it off?
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经晕船，是否好奇过是什么原因导致的，以及有什么办法可以缓解或预防吗？

sentences.en: Joining me today is Dr. Arnon Rolnick, a clinical and experimental psychologist from
sentences.zh: 今天来到节目中的是来自以色列的临床与实验心理学家阿农·罗尔尼克博士，

sentences.en: Israel, where he directs Rolnick's Institute for Advanced Psychotherapy and studies psychophysiology and the integration of technology and psychology.
sentences.zh: 他在那里负责罗尔尼克高级心理治疗研究所，并研究心理生理学以及技术与心理学的融合。

sentences.en: He spent 20 years as a psychologist in the Israeli
sentences.zh: 他曾在以色列海军担任了20年的心理学家，

sentences.en: Navy, developing various methods to improve sailors' performance and well-being under conditions that tended to make them seasick.
sentences.zh: 开发了多种方法来改善水兵在容易导致晕船的环境下的表现和身心健康。

sentences.en: He is also working on a book exploring how virtual psychotherapy can open new ways to study the roles of the body and brain in therapy.
sentences.zh: 他目前还在撰写一本书，探讨虚拟心理治疗如何开辟研究身体和大脑在治疗中作用的新途径。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Rolnick.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，罗尔尼克博士。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for inviting me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢您的邀请。

sentences.en: One reason I wanted to talk to you today is to learn more about one of the papers you're presenting in at APA's Technology, Mind, and Society conference.
sentences.zh: 我今天想和您交流的一个原因是，想更多地了解您在美国心理学会“技术、思维与社会”会议上发表的一篇论文。

sentences.en: It's called Technology Made Us Motion Sick,
sentences.zh: 题目是《技术让我们晕动，

sentences.en: Autonomous Cars Will Make Us Vomit.
sentences.zh: 自动驾驶汽车会让我们呕吐》。

sentences.en: It's a review of 40 years of research, which is a lot of time to study motion sickness.
sentences.zh: 这是一篇回顾了40年研究成果的综述，研究晕动症的时间跨度相当长。

sentences.en: With the advent of self-driving cars, the idea that these vehicles might make people motion sick is one glitch that hasn't gotten a lot of coverage by the media.
sentences.zh: 随着自动驾驶汽车的出现，这些车辆可能会导致人们晕动症，这是媒体尚未充分报道的一个小故障。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering, how much do scientists know at this point about the likelihood that this will be a widespread problem, and what can we do about it?
sentences.zh: 所以我很想知道，科学家们目前对这是否会成为一个普遍问题了解多少？我们又能做些什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, we studied this phenomena for many years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们研究这种现象已经很多年了。

sentences.en: In fact, this is one of the ancient problems that technology made.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是技术带来的古老问题之一。

sentences.en: You know, we were very happy that we could be moved by cars, ships, and horses,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们曾为能乘坐汽车、轮船和马车出行而感到非常高兴，

sentences.en: but we were not aware that it will produce such a debilitating effect like motion sickness.
sentences.zh: 但我们并没有意识到它会产生像晕动症这样令人衰弱的影响。

sentences.en: And not only, we found in my book in the Navy that people tend to be even helpless.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，我在海军的研究中发现，人们甚至会感到无助。

sentences.en: They feel desperate.
sentences.zh: 他们感到绝望。

sentences.en: And I connected it to Martin Zelligman's theory of learned helplessness.
sentences.zh: 我将其与马丁·塞利格曼的习得性无助理论联系了起来。

sentences.en: The exposure to uncontrolled motion is producing some sickness.
sentences.zh: 暴露在无法控制的运动中会产生某种不适感。

sentences.en: And not only sickness, it produced really some type of depression, which I was able to show in my research.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是不适，它确实产生了一种抑郁感，我在研究中也证实了这一点。

sentences.en: So that brought me to the question,
sentences.zh: 这引出了一个问题：

sentences.en: how comes that are certain people who are not sick, like drivers.
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人不会晕，比如驾驶员？

sentences.en: And that came very nice with the theory that controllability, what learned helplessness theory predicts, controllability prevents feeling bad.
sentences.zh: 这与习得性无助理论的预测非常吻合，即“可控性”可以防止产生糟糕的感觉。

sentences.en: So I did this study for almost 40 years ago, and I was not aware at that time that in few years years from now, everybody will be passenger.
sentences.zh: 所以我大约在40年前做了这项研究，当时我并没有意识到，几年后的今天，每个人都将成为乘客。

sentences.en: And not only they will be passenger, they will be reading devices like phones or Kindle, because they are free, they don't have to drive.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不仅是乘客，还会因为空闲而阅读手机或Kindle等设备，因为他们不需要开车。

sentences.en: So this autonomous car or driveless car is opening a real problem or producing a real problem, which we psychologists will have to deal deal with.
sentences.zh: 所以这种自动驾驶汽车或无人驾驶汽车正在引发一个真正的问题，这是我们心理学家必须去应对的。

sentences.en: And I'm going to present a few types of solutions or possible solutions, which I did in my work in the Navy.
sentences.zh: 我将在会上介绍我在海军工作中总结出的几种解决方案或可能的解决途径。

sentences.en: One of them was artificial horizon.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是人工地平线。

sentences.en: We do know that the reason motion sickness developed, it has to do with some type of conflict between the information the eyes get and the information
sentences.zh: 我们知道晕动症产生的原因，与眼睛获取的信息和

sentences.en: that the vestibular information or vestibular system.
sentences.zh: 前庭系统获取的信息之间存在某种冲突有关。

sentences.en: Which is in your ear?
sentences.zh: 是在耳朵里吗？

sentences.en: In our inner ear, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，在我们的内耳里。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in the study I did with the TNO in the Netherlands, we were able to show that using artificial horizon, we could dramatically reduce the amount of motion sickness and increase
sentences.zh: 在我和荷兰TNO机构合作的研究中，我们能够证明，使用人工地平线可以显著减少晕动症的发生，并提高

sentences.en: performance, that performance is becoming better, as compared to people who did not have this
sentences.zh: 表现。与没有使用这种人工地平线的人相比，他们的表现更好，

sentences.en: artificial horizon, which was kind of projected on the walls of the tilting room that we use.
sentences.zh: 这种人工地平线是投射在我们使用的倾斜室墙壁上的。

sentences.en: But this is some technical details.
sentences.zh: 不过这些是一些技术细节。

sentences.en: But what I really want to emphasize in this lecture that I'm going to give, which will be one of another two lectures.
sentences.zh: 但我真正想在这次演讲中强调的是——我还有另外两场演讲——

sentences.en: But one of my talks will speak not so much on technical solution, but that we as psychologists have to examine the process of adaptation.
sentences.zh: 其中一场演讲不会过多谈论技术解决方案，而是强调我们作为心理学家必须审视“适应过程”。

sentences.en: Because people do adapt to motion sickness, but we don't know enough about this process.
sentences.zh: 因为人们确实会对晕动症产生适应，但我们对这个过程了解得还不够。

sentences.en: And apparently it's not enough just to be exposed to the motion.
sentences.zh: 显然，仅仅暴露在运动中是不够的。

sentences.en: We have to help them using various cognitive behavioural therapy approaches.
sentences.zh: 我们必须利用各种认知行为疗法来帮助他们。

sentences.en: And there is an interesting correlation now between what I do in my clinical practice with people who are afraid from being sick or afraid from vomiting.
sentences.zh: 目前我临床实践中治疗那些害怕晕车或害怕呕吐的人的方法，与此之间存在有趣的关联。

sentences.en: I'm doing gradual exposure to motion sickness.
sentences.zh: 我正在对他们进行晕动症的渐进式暴露疗法。

sentences.en: And it is possible that if with this driverless car, we will need to do the same.
sentences.zh: 很有可能，对于无人驾驶汽车，我们也需要这样做。

sentences.en: So this is one of the area I'm going to talk in this conference.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我将在本次会议上讨论的领域之一。

sentences.en: But then I will jump, if it's okay with you, to another area which related to my main practice as a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，我想跳到另一个与我作为临床心理学家的主要工作相关的领域。

sentences.en: Okay, but before we get too far into that, a couple of questions about motion sickness.
sentences.zh: 好的，但在深入探讨之前，还有几个关于晕动症的问题。

sentences.en: So you talked about an artificial horizon.
sentences.zh: 您刚才提到了人工地平线。

sentences.en: So I'm in an autonomous car.
sentences.zh: 如果我坐在自动驾驶汽车里，

sentences.en: There's a real horizon out there.
sentences.zh: 外面有真实的地平线。

sentences.en: So why does that not prevent me from getting motion sick?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么它不能防止我晕车呢？

sentences.en: What's happening?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Or if you just gave me a steering wheel, and I thought I was in control, would I feel better?
sentences.zh: 或者，如果您给我一个方向盘，让我以为自己在掌控，我会感觉好些吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's a very interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这非常有趣。

sentences.en: You have two points here.
sentences.zh: 您提到了两点。

sentences.en: Both of them are good.
sentences.zh: 两点都很好。

sentences.en: But let's go to the second one, which I was just trying in my clinic in Israel.
sentences.zh: 但让我们谈谈第二点，我刚才在以色列的诊所里尝试过。

sentences.en: I wondered what happened if you have a wheel, but you don't really control, you just play with it, like what I did with my child when he was some years ago.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，如果你有一个方向盘，但并没有真正控制它，只是像我几年前陪孩子玩那样摆弄它，会怎样？

sentences.en: And apparently, we don't have a good research about it yet.
sentences.zh: 显然，我们目前还没有关于此的深入研究。

sentences.en: But apparently, it does help.
sentences.zh: 但看起来它确实有帮助。

sentences.en: So, you know, in this autonomous car, there's going to be some stages.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在自动驾驶汽车中，会有几个阶段。

sentences.en: At the beginning, we will still need the wheel, although it would not really control the car.
sentences.zh: 起初，我们仍然需要方向盘，尽管它并不能真正控制汽车。

sentences.en: So I do suggest that people will kind of play with a useless wheel, just to feel that have perceived control.
sentences.zh: 所以我建议人们可以摆弄一个无用的方向盘，只是为了获得一种“感知控制感”。

sentences.en: Regarding your previous question, it is true.
sentences.zh: 关于您之前的问题，确实如此。

sentences.en: The main focus is that we need to give them a good visual reference.
sentences.zh: 重点在于我们需要给他们提供良好的视觉参考。

sentences.en: If the car manufacturer will be wise enough, they will do a big windows, and that will be beSt. But if you will notice in the diagram of how do they prepare or plan
sentences.zh: 如果汽车制造商足够聪明，他们会设计大窗户，那是最好的。但如果你注意一下他们准备或规划这些汽车的图表，

sentences.en: those car, they are going to be like a room with many chairs facing each other, not facing the movement, and a lot of screens.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来就像一个房间，里面有很多椅子面对面摆放，而不是面向行驶方向，而且还有很多屏幕。

sentences.en: So people might not see the visual surrounding.
sentences.zh: 所以人们可能看不到周围的视觉环境。

sentences.en: And this is why I'm kind of,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我有点……

sentences.en: I think that they will have to hear us, psychologists.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们必须听取我们心理学家的意见。

sentences.en: We psychologists, our voice must be heard in these issues.
sentences.zh: 我们心理学家的声音必须在这些问题上被听到。

sentences.en: Is that a problem so far with the cars that they're designing?
sentences.zh: 目前设计的汽车是否存在这个问题？

sentences.en: Are you hearing that car sickness is an issue?
sentences.zh: 您是否听说晕车是一个问题？

sentences.en: Well, you see, everybody is now obsessed with the issue, shall they do accident or not?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，大家现在都沉迷于这个问题：它们会不会发生事故？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And not enough about this issue.
sentences.zh: 而对这个问题关注不够。

sentences.en: Well, there is, I should be more concrete, or
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实有，我应该说得更具体一点，或者

sentences.en: Mercedes-Benz is doing some research, and other companies are doing research.
sentences.zh: 梅赛德斯-奔驰正在做一些研究，其他公司也在做研究。

sentences.en: So it's not that they ignore it.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是他们忽略了这一点。

sentences.en: But still, the main focus is not exactly on this issue, I think.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，重点确实没有完全放在这个问题上。

sentences.en: There is another issue I should mention, it's again important for psychologists, the issue of truSt. We have to trust this computer that will drive us.
sentences.zh: 还有一个问题我应该提一下，这对心理学家来说同样重要，那就是信任问题。我们必须信任这台将要驾驶我们的计算机。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it will be interesting to see what type of people will be kind of trusting it, no problem.
sentences.zh: 看看哪些人会毫无问题地信任它，这会很有趣。

sentences.en: And other who will sit anxious, and anxiety might produce even more sickness.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人会坐得焦虑不安，焦虑可能会导致更严重的晕动症。

sentences.en: So there's interesting questions here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有很多有趣的问题。

sentences.en: So why is it that some people get seasick or carsick, and others don't?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么有些人会晕船或晕车，而另一些人不会呢？

sentences.en: That's again a good question.
sentences.zh: 这又是一个好问题。

sentences.en: Some people thought it's related to their, to the function of their vestibular system in the inner area.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为这与他们内耳前庭系统的功能有关。

sentences.en: And apparently not.
sentences.zh: 但显然不是。

sentences.en: Everybody that has a functional vestibular system might get sick.
sentences.zh: 任何拥有正常前庭系统的人都可能晕动。

sentences.en: In our Navy, my data show that 70% of the people get seasick if their sea is high enough.
sentences.zh: 在我们的海军中，我的数据显示，如果海浪足够大，70%的人会晕船。

sentences.en: In the car, it might be a little bit less, it might be less.
sentences.zh: 在汽车里，比例可能会低一些，可能会低一些。

sentences.en: But again, if they will be reading and looking on certain devices, they will be apparently either not sick, or they will have what they call sopite syndrome.
sentences.zh: 但同样，如果他们一直在阅读或盯着某些设备看，显然他们要么会晕，要么会出现所谓的“嗜睡综合征”。

sentences.en: Sopite syndrome is related to what I said about some type of lethargy, apathy, depression, that we did show that a motion sickness does produce, even without nausea.
sentences.zh: 嗜睡综合征与我刚才提到的那种昏睡、冷漠、抑郁有关，我们已经证明晕动症即使在没有恶心的情况下也会产生这种症状。

sentences.en: So that's produced, it's not something that you have before you get motion sick.
sentences.zh: 所以这是产生的后果，并不是你在晕动症发作前就有的。

sentences.en: It's when, after you become motion sick, you have this sopite syndrome.
sentences.zh: 是在你晕动之后，才会出现这种嗜睡综合征。

sentences.en: That's an interesting question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: I studied with three of the leading people in this field.
sentences.zh: 我曾与该领域的三位领军人物一起研究过。

sentences.en: One is
sentences.zh: 一位是

sentences.en: J.T.
sentences.zh: J.T.

sentences.en: Reason from England.
sentences.zh: 里森（Reason），来自英国。

sentences.en: The other is Ashton Grabeil from Florida.
sentences.zh: 另一位是来自佛罗里达的阿什顿·格雷比尔（Ashton Graybiel）。

sentences.en: And the third is James Lackner in Brandeis University.
sentences.zh: 第三位是布兰迪斯大学的詹姆斯·拉克纳（James Lackner）。

sentences.en: They were all studying this sopite syndrome.
sentences.zh: 他们都在研究这种嗜睡综合征。

sentences.en: And they say that sometimes it develops even without the symptoms of motion sickness.
sentences.zh: 他们说，有时它甚至在没有晕动症症状的情况下也会发展出来。

sentences.en: Like we can see it as a phenomenon that might be developed without nausea and without vomiting.
sentences.zh: 我们可以将其视为一种可能在没有恶心和呕吐的情况下发展的现象。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So you talked a little bit about cognitive behavioral therapy as one way to counteract motion sickness.
sentences.zh: 您刚才谈到认知行为疗法是抵消晕动症的一种方法。

sentences.en: How exactly would that work?
sentences.zh: 这具体是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: Well, in my studies, again, some earlier studies and some later, uh, we trained, uh, uh, soldier or sailors, uh, with some cognitive, simple cognitive behavioral, uh, techniques,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我的研究中，包括一些早期和后期的研究，我们用一些简单的认知行为技术训练士兵或水兵，

sentences.en: or it could be either relaxation, either changing their cognition.
sentences.zh: 可以是放松训练，也可以是改变他们的认知。

sentences.en: And we show that people that did it or, and that people that had high self-control were by far, they perform better than their, uh,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些进行了训练的人，或者那些具有高自我控制力的人，他们的表现远好于他们的

sentences.en: counterparts or their, uh, other, uh, sailors that did not have self-control ability.
sentences.zh: 同行，或者那些没有自我控制能力的其他水兵。

sentences.en: We use the classical, uh, method of measuring self-control.
sentences.zh: 我们使用了测量自我控制力的经典方法。

sentences.en: And, uh, we were able to show that, uh, cognitive ability of, uh, self-control might be very useful.
sentences.zh: 我们能够证明，自我控制的认知能力可能非常有用。

sentences.en: Now I should mention here a very, uh, important figure.
sentences.zh: 这里我必须提到一位非常重要的人物。

sentences.en: His name is Dobby, James Dobby, I believe, uh, who worked in the Naval Biodynamic Lab here in this country.
sentences.zh: 他的名字是多比（Dobby），詹姆斯·多比，我想，他曾在这个国家的海军生物动力实验室工作。

sentences.en: And he just published a book about his, I am speaking about 40 years.
sentences.zh: 他刚刚出版了一本关于他工作的书，我说的是40年的经验。

sentences.en: I think he's working
sentences.zh: 我想他已经工作了

sentences.en: 50 years in the field and he is not psychologist, but what he found that in order to help pilots,
sentences.zh: 50年，他不是心理学家，但他发现为了帮助飞行员、

sentences.en: sailors, and people, uh, that suffer from motion sickness, he uses cognitive behavioral therapies.
sentences.zh: 水兵以及那些患有晕动症的人，他使用了认知行为疗法。

sentences.en: And there is another study that people did it in the sea just, uh, some years ago with very good results.
sentences.zh: 还有另一项研究，几年前人们在海上进行了同样的尝试，效果非常好。

sentences.en: So yes, we, uh, you know, people in the field of cognitive behavioral therapy usually think that
sentences.zh: 所以是的，你知道，认知行为疗法领域的人通常认为

sentences.en: their job is to prevent, uh, driver's rage or driver's anger or, uh, you know, anxiety or depression.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作是防止路怒症、愤怒，或者焦虑、抑郁。

sentences.en: Uh, I, uh, invite our colleague in the CBT to begin to prepare themselves to a new arena that they should, uh, work.
sentences.zh: 我邀请我们在CBT领域的同事开始为他们即将投入的新领域做好准备。

sentences.en: And this is how to help people at the cars.
sentences.zh: 那就是如何帮助车里的人。

sentences.en: And more important,
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，

sentences.en: motion sickness is very much, uh, conditioned.
sentences.zh: 晕动症在很大程度上是条件反射性的。

sentences.en: Like if I'm driving in a car and in this car, there is a smell, some type of smell that usually wouldn't bother me.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我开车时车里有一种气味，这种气味通常不会困扰我。

sentences.en: This smell is kind of conditioned with the nausea.
sentences.zh: 但这种气味会与恶心产生条件反射。

sentences.en: This is a phenomenon we all know in psychology, we called conditioned taste aversion and conditioned smell aversion.
sentences.zh: 这是心理学中众所周知的现象，我们称之为条件性味觉厌恶和条件性嗅觉厌恶。

sentences.en: So it is possible again that we might also test the, the role of odors and maybe we can prevent, uh, this conditioning by using different odors at the first, uh, uh,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们再次测试气味的作用是可能的，也许我们可以通过在最初使用不同的气味来防止这种条件反射。

sentences.en: drive or the first voyage that people are doing.
sentences.zh: 驾驶或人们正在进行的第一次航行。

sentences.en: So you'd associate a good odor with feeling well.
sentences.zh: 所以你会把好闻的气味与感觉良好联系起来。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But Mary and I go to other field that I'm like, I began with the old
sentences.zh: 但玛丽和我转向了另一个领域，我开始处理的是旧的

sentences.en: ancient problem, but now I'm dealing a lot with, uh, the role of the internet in helping people.
sentences.zh: 古老的问题，但现在我处理很多关于互联网在帮助人们方面的作用。

sentences.en: Um, and in fact, in psychology, there is two directions that the internet took.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实上，在心理学领域，互联网的发展有两个方向。

sentences.en: One is to do what they call Skype therapy or online video conference.
sentences.zh: 一个是进行所谓的Skype治疗或在线视频会议。

sentences.en: And this is mainly the relational people or the psychodynamic people that said, Hey, it's interesting to see what we can learn, uh, about therapy when we do it online.
sentences.zh: 这主要是那些关注关系或心理动力学的人说的，嘿，看看我们在网上进行治疗时能学到什么，这很有趣。

sentences.en: Is it the same therapy?
sentences.zh: 这是同样的治疗吗？

sentences.en: Is it the same alliance that is produced in this online therapy?
sentences.zh: 这种在线治疗中产生的联盟是同样的吗？

sentences.en: And I just published a book with
sentences.zh: 我刚刚出版了一本书，作者是

sentences.en: Chaim Weinberg, a friend of mine about online therapy.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友Chaim Weinberg，关于在线治疗的。

sentences.en: There is some books in this area, but our book
sentences.zh: 这个领域有一些书，但我们的书

sentences.en: is dealing with cases that we are doing it not only one-on-one like classical psychotherapy, we are doing it with couples, with families, with groups, and with organizations.
sentences.zh: 处理的案例不仅仅像传统的心理治疗那样是一对一的，我们还与夫妻、家庭、团体和组织一起进行。

sentences.en: So this is the uniqueness of our book, that we are dealing it, doing online therapy, uh, and that produce a very interesting questions.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们书的独特之处，我们正在处理、进行在线治疗，这产生了一些非常有趣的问题。

sentences.en: For example, now there's two people sitting in front of me, you and our technician.
sentences.zh: 例如，现在有两个人坐在我面前，你和我们的技术员。

sentences.en: And, uh, suppose I want to see the interaction between the two of you.
sentences.zh: 而且，假设我想看看你们两人之间的互动。

sentences.en: Now, the classical people just put the guy or the couple before the camera, before the computer, and we just see two faces.
sentences.zh: 现在，传统的人只是把那个人或那对夫妇放在摄像机前，放在电脑前，我们只能看到两张脸。

sentences.en: It's not what we want.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们想要的。

sentences.en: We want to see the full body.
sentences.zh: 我们想看到全身。

sentences.en: We want to see the interaction between the couple.
sentences.zh: 我们想看到夫妻之间的互动。

sentences.en: What happens when the wife says something that bothers the, the, the, the male or vice versa.
sentences.zh: 当妻子说了什么让男性感到困扰时会发生什么，反之亦然。

sentences.en: We want to see their bodily behavior.
sentences.zh: 我们想看到他们的肢体行为。

sentences.en: So we did, uh, develop some new way that, uh, with the new, uh, new cameras that can go from one to the other.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实开发了一些新方法，利用新的摄像机，可以在一个人和另一个人之间切换。

sentences.en: And the, the couple then can also see where I'm looking, although I'm in Israel.
sentences.zh: 而且这对夫妇也可以看到我在看哪里，尽管我在以色列。

sentences.en: And the couple, let's say, is in the United States.
sentences.zh: 而这对夫妇，比方说，在美国。

sentences.en: We found the cameras that could, uh, represent, uh, my head.
sentences.zh: 我们找到了可以代表我头部的摄像机。

sentences.en: And now my head is showing the camera is looking on you.
sentences.zh: 现在我的头部显示摄像机正在看着你。

sentences.en: And now the camera is looking on our nice technician here.
sentences.zh: 现在摄像机正在看着我们这位优秀的技术员。

sentences.en: So, uh, I'm, I'm speaking about a lot of things that we are testing now regarding this online therapy.
sentences.zh: 所以，我正在谈论我们现在正在测试的关于这种在线治疗的很多事情。

sentences.en: So is the therapist controlling the, the cameras and then the people who are the, the patients, they're able to see themselves at the same time or afterwards?
sentences.zh: 那么是治疗师在控制摄像机，然后作为病人的那些人，他们能够同时或事后看到自己吗？

sentences.en: How, how exactly does that work?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: Well, the, the, uh, people can see themselves.
sentences.zh: 嗯，人们可以看到他们自己。

sentences.en: That's another interesting question in this
sentences.zh: 这是这个领域另一个有趣的问题

sentences.en: Skype and zoom and all of the other, uh, uh, programs, people can see themselves and sometimes it's produced some, uh, too much people are too much self-aware.
sentences.zh: Skype、Zoom和所有其他程序，人们可以看到自己，有时这会产生一些过度的自我意识。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But your question is very important.
sentences.zh: 但你的问题非常重要。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We found a way that the therapist from a distance can control the camera, which exists in the couple's room.
sentences.zh: 我们找到了一种方法，让远方的治疗师可以控制存在于夫妻房间里的摄像机。

sentences.en: And in this way, it makes it somewhat more like a real therapy, you know, in couple therapy, we usually need to kind of approach the male and tell him, Hey, please calm down.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，它让治疗变得更像真实的治疗，你知道，在夫妻治疗中，我们通常需要接近男性并告诉他，嘿，请冷静下来。

sentences.en: We might approach the, the female and tell her, could you invite him in more?
sentences.zh: 我们可能会接近女性并告诉她，你能多邀请他参与进来吗？

sentences.en: So it is, we are like a conductor of, uh, uh, uh, uh, orchestra and, uh, we cannot do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就像管弦乐队的指挥，我们做不到。

sentences.en: Well, we couldn't do it till we develop this technique where we can really give the, the, the, the, the, the couple the feeling that we
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我们开发出这种技术之前我们做不到，通过这种技术，我们真的可以给夫妻一种感觉，即我们

sentences.en: are either looking on one of them or the other.
sentences.zh: 要么在看着他们中的一个，要么在看着另一个。

sentences.en: So that's one direction that we are doing with online therapy, but that's not enough.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们在线治疗的一个方向，但这还不够。

sentences.en: Uh, I think that, uh, um, we need not to, uh, it's not enough to be happy that we are doing a good online therapy.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我们不需要，仅仅因为我们正在进行良好的在线治疗而感到高兴是不够的。

sentences.en: What happens between one session to the other session?
sentences.zh: 在一次治疗和下一次治疗之间会发生什么？

sentences.en: Usually in psychotherapy, psychotherapy is a wonderful experience.
sentences.zh: 通常在心理治疗中，心理治疗是一种美妙的体验。

sentences.en: People love it.
sentences.zh: 人们喜欢它。

sentences.en: If we are a good psychotherapist, uh, the patient feels that you understand him.
sentences.zh: 如果我们是一位优秀的心理治疗师，病人会觉得你理解他。

sentences.en: The patient feels that you are helping him to accept himself.
sentences.zh: 病人会觉得你在帮助他接纳自己。

sentences.en: The patient might feel some hope.
sentences.zh: 病人可能会感到一些希望。

sentences.en: It's a wonderful thing, but it's a fantasy that we can think that in one session a week or two sessions a week, we can really do a significant change.
sentences.zh: 这是一件美妙的事情，但认为我们每周一次或两次治疗就能真正产生重大改变是一种幻想。

sentences.en: So we developed an application that is kind of, um, accompanying the subject or the patient all the week.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开发了一个应用程序，它有点像是在整个星期陪伴着受试者或病人。

sentences.en: Suppose we were talking about, let's say, my arousal now, speaking in this conference.
sentences.zh: 假设我们正在谈论，比方说，我现在在这个会议上发言时的唤醒状态。

sentences.en: And, uh, I will come to my therapist and I say, I was a little bit too, uh,
sentences.zh: 而且，我会去找我的治疗师说，我有点太，嗯，

sentences.en: I don't know, exhausted.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: And suppose the therapist say, listen, now, no, it's okay.
sentences.zh: 假设治疗师说，听着，现在，不，没关系。

sentences.en: You can take breath and you can, uh, uh, kind of think differently, you know, cognitive, but that's not enough.
sentences.zh: 你可以深呼吸，你可以换个角度思考，你知道，认知上的，但这还不够。

sentences.en: What will happen when I'm going to be interviewed tomorrow to the CBS?
sentences.zh: 当我明天去CBS接受采访时会发生什么？

sentences.en: I might, it, it might happen again.
sentences.zh: 它可能会再次发生。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So our point is that we will, between session, we produced an application that reminds me to do what we discussed.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的观点是，在治疗之间，我们制作了一个应用程序，提醒我做我们讨论过的事情。

sentences.en: It could be some types of what we call in CBT homework, but it could also be some type of, hey, Arnon, why won't you, this program kind of, uh, uh,
sentences.zh: 这可能是一些我们在CBT中所谓的家庭作业，但也可能是一些，嘿，Arnon，为什么你不，这个程序有点像，嗯，

sentences.en: accompany, I would say, why won't you share with me some of your dreams or some of the thoughts that you had in the middle of the week?
sentences.zh: 陪伴，我会说，为什么你不和我分享一些你的梦，或者你在周中产生的一些想法呢？

sentences.en: So our idea is to produce, uh, we produced, uh, application that is accompanying the subject of between sessions.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的想法是制作，我们制作了一个应用程序，在治疗之间陪伴着受试者。

sentences.en: It also measures our anxiety, our depression.
sentences.zh: 它还测量我们的焦虑、我们的抑郁。

sentences.en: So there is a constant measure of the patient's situation, the patient's wellbeing,
sentences.zh: 所以有一个对病人状况、病人幸福感的持续测量，

sentences.en: and that helps the therapist to, uh, uh, be aware what's happening and if the therapy is going well or not.
sentences.zh: 这有助于治疗师意识到正在发生什么，以及治疗是否进展顺利。

sentences.en: So how is it measuring these things?
sentences.zh: 那么它是如何测量这些东西的呢？

sentences.en: Is it like take, take testing your, um, skin conductance or your heart rate or, I mean, what, what exactly is it doing?
sentences.zh: 它是像测试你的皮肤电导或心率吗，或者，我是说，它到底在做什么？

sentences.en: And then like, as you said it so that every day at three o'clock, it reminds you like now's the time for you to be mindful and deep, deep breathe and all those good things.
sentences.zh: 然后就像你说的，每天三点钟，它提醒你现在是时候保持正念、深呼吸以及所有那些好事了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Reminder is, is of course, one very important aspect.
sentences.zh: 提醒当然是一个非常重要的方面。

sentences.en: We came from the biofeedback field, all of our, uh, it's not only me, it's, uh, uh, Dr. Yuvalo dead and, uh, Dror Gronich, who is kind of developing this system.
sentences.zh: 我们来自生物反馈领域，我们所有的，不仅仅是我，还有Yuvalo博士和Dror Gronich，他们正在开发这个系统。

sentences.en: So we are very much aware of the, uh, psychophysiology and the sensor.
sentences.zh: 所以我们非常了解心理生理学和传感器。

sentences.en: But at this stage, we are more focusing really on, on some interaction between the patient and the therapiSt. And it's, it's, it's going automatically.
sentences.zh: 但在现阶段，我们更多地专注于病人和治疗师之间的一些互动。而且它是自动进行的。

sentences.en: The therapist does not have to be aware, Hey, what happens to my, uh, patient who now in Tel Aviv, the system, send him,
sentences.zh: 治疗师不必意识到，嘿，现在在特拉维夫的病人发生了什么，系统会发送给他，

sentences.en: uh, uh, a message, a message that is designed with the therapist and the patient.
sentences.zh: 一条信息，一条由治疗师和病人共同设计的信息。

sentences.en: Let's say this week, we are going to focus on your ability, uh, uh, to think differently on, on your ability to initiate, uh, more, um, social activities.
sentences.zh: 比方说这周，我们将专注于你换个角度思考的能力，专注于你发起更多社交活动的能力。

sentences.en: So it's, uh, so coming back to your question, it's not mainly sensors, although we have developed some ideas about sensors, but at this stage, it is, uh, more verbal.
sentences.zh: 所以，回到你的问题，它主要不是传感器，尽管我们已经开发了一些关于传感器的想法，但在现阶段，它更多是口头的。

sentences.en: So you think that's where psychotherapy is going, or is this going to be just an adjunct to traditional therapy?
sentences.zh: 所以你认为这就是心理治疗的发展方向，还是这只会成为传统治疗的辅助手段？

sentences.en: I think we psychologists are now, uh, divided to two, uh, um, companies or no, two camps.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们心理学家现在分成了两个阵营。

sentences.en: There is the camp who say, this is not psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 有一个阵营说，这不是心理治疗。

sentences.en: We are not allowed to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们不允许这样做。

sentences.en: The main issue in psychotherapy is the human interaction.
sentences.zh: 心理治疗的核心问题是人际互动。

sentences.en: And they say, completely don't do that.
sentences.zh: 他们说，完全不要那样做。

sentences.en: There is the other camp who say, if it works, why won't we do it?
sentences.zh: 另一个阵营说，如果它有效，为什么我们不做呢？

sentences.en: In my clinic, we decided to, uh, combine the two, uh, uh, camps.
sentences.zh: 在我的诊所，我们决定将这两个阵营结合起来。

sentences.en: And what we are doing is really, we are doing a lot of online therapy and coming back to your question.
sentences.zh: 我们正在做的是，我们确实在进行大量的在线治疗，回到你的问题。

sentences.en: We are going there.
sentences.zh: 我们正在朝着那个方向发展。

sentences.en: No, the genie is out of the battle.
sentences.zh: 不，精灵已经从瓶子里出来了。

sentences.en: Now we could use it in a positive way or a negative way.
sentences.zh: 现在我们可以以积极的方式或消极的方式使用它。

sentences.en: I've just been in New York and I've seen
sentences.zh: 我刚去过纽约，看了

sentences.en: Aladdin and we could see, uh, that there was happy end there.
sentences.zh: 《阿拉丁》，我们可以看到那里有一个圆满的结局。

sentences.en: And I do hope that in our case, there will also be some happy end, namely that psychotherapy can really advance using
sentences.zh: 我确实希望在我们的案例中，也会有一些圆满的结局，即心理治疗可以通过使用

sentences.en: both online video conference and online applications that can enhance the therapy.
sentences.zh: 在线视频会议和可以增强治疗效果的在线应用程序来真正进步。

sentences.en: Well, it sounds like you're doing a lot of really interesting work in, in your clinic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，听起来你在诊所里做了很多非常有趣的工作。

sentences.en: I'm very happy that you were able to join us today and appreciate your taking the time.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你今天能加入我们，并感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: And, um, we'll keep an eye on, on your work.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们会密切关注你的工作。

sentences.en: I'm sure people who, uh, experience things like seasickness and car sickness are going to be very concerned as we have more and more of these autonomous cars out there.
sentences.zh: 我相信那些经历过晕船和晕车的人会非常担心，因为我们有越来越多的自动驾驶汽车。

sentences.en: So I hope that your work is able to, uh, save those of us who get a little queasy from experiencing that.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你的工作能够拯救我们这些容易感到恶心的人，免受那种体验。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，谢谢。

sentences.en: And, uh, uh, uh, if people are interested, uh, uh, uh, our work will be published in a site called, uh, internet psychology, uh, sorry, internet psychotherapy dot org,
sentences.zh: 而且，如果人们感兴趣，我们的工作将发布在一个名为internetpsychology，抱歉，internetpsychotherapy.org的网站上，

sentences.en: internet psychotherapy, one word dot org.
sentences.zh: internetpsychotherapy，一个词，点org。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: That's good to know.
sentences.zh: 很高兴知道这一点。

sentences.en: We can include that in our notes.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把它包含在我们的笔记中。

sentences.en: So, uh, before we go, I just wanted to remind our listeners that we at speaking of psychology want to hear from you.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们结束之前，我只想提醒我们的听众，我们《心理学谈话》节目想听到你们的声音。

sentences.en: You can email your comments and ideas to speaking of psychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过电子邮件将你的评论和想法发送到speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: That's speaking of psychology, all one word dot org.
sentences.zh: 那是speakingofpsychology，全部连在一起，点org。

sentences.en: And please give us a rating in iTunes.
sentences.zh: 请在iTunes上给我们评分。

sentences.en: It really helps.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is part of the APA podcast network, which includes other informative
sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》是APA播客网络的一部分，该网络还包括其他信息丰富的

sentences.en: podcasts, such as APA journals, dialogue about new psychological research and progress notes about the practice of psychology.
sentences.zh: 播客，例如《APA期刊》，关于新心理学研究的对话，以及关于心理学实践的进度记录。

sentences.en: You can find all our podcasts on Apple, Stitcher, Spotify, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Apple、Stitcher、Spotify或任何你获取播客的地方找到我们所有的播客。

sentences.en: You can also go to our website, www.speakingofpsychology.org and listen to more episodes.
sentences.zh: 你也可以访问我们的网站www.speakingofpsychology.org并收听更多剧集。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills with the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 我是美国心理学会的Kim Mills。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
